title: Rules, discretion and market stabilisation in the euro area
summary_en: How much should ECB market-stabilisation tools (SMP, OMT, PEPP, TPI) be governed by hard rules vs. operational discretion? Darvas and Papadia compare the four instruments and argue that ambiguity in the design of access criteria has both helped (deterring speculation) and hurt (raising uncertainty for member-state debt management). Prepared for the European Parliament's ECON committee, the report calibrates the rules-vs-discretion balance for each tool and recommends modest tightening of the access framework on TPI specifically.
policy_relevance: Directly relevant for Hungarian fiscal-policy planning (NGM, ÁKK) and for MNB's monitoring of euro-area sovereign-spread dynamics. Hungary, while outside the euro, is sensitive to euro-area sovereign-stress episodes via cross-border bank funding and contagion through CEE risk premia. The paper provides the analytical case for a more transparent TPI access framework — an outcome Hungary would benefit from indirectly via more stable ECB-policy expectations.
